correctness.rationale: The target masses are (1-p)(1-q),p+q-2pq,pq. Direct mass subtraction yields errors pq for Bin(1,p+q-pq) and (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2 for Bin(2,sqrt(pq)). If pq>=1/4, ordering p>=q implies q>=1/4 and the second error <=1/4, with equality only p=1,q=1/4. At that pair, for every m>=2 the largest possible Bin(m,r) probability at 1 is (1-1/m)^(m-1)<=1/2 whereas target P(1)=3/4; for m=1 mass at 2 is 0 vs 1/4. This proves the unrestricted lower bound and unique extremizers, not pointwise best m for all pairs.
